rule: The red shape slides toward the 2x2 grey block until it touches it, and the grey block is reshaped into the mirror image of the red shape reflected across the contact line.
gap: Move-until-contact exists, but chaining it with reshaping the target object into the reflected copy of the mover is missing.

rule: Every square object (equal height and width, solid or hollow, any size/colour) gets red marks on the two cells orthogonally outside each of its four bbox corners; non-square objects are unchanged.
gap: Behaviour keys need a colour- and size-independent shape class 'is square (h==w)' so corner marks generalise to unseen colour/size.

rule: Each multi-colour template shape contains one anchor-coloured cell; copies of the template are stamped at every isolated cell of that anchor colour, the original template is erased, and grey noise cells are deleted.
gap: No operator to stamp a template object at all marker cells matching its anchor colour (copy-to-marker), with template removal.

rule: Remove the plus-shaped object and paint the centre cell of every odd-sided square of the main colour with the plus's colour; even-sided squares stay unchanged.
gap: Mark colour comes from an indicator plus that varies per demo; also needs 'centre of odd square' for unseen sizes (7x7).

rule: The grid is three 5x5 panels split by magenta lines, each holding one object; output is a 5x5 panel where the objects are stacked bottom-up in panel order (left panel lowest), keeping their columns, rows packed with no gaps.
gap: Panels are split, but output needs vertical concatenation/stacking of each panel's object rows, not a cellwise vote or overlay.

rule: Crop the grey mask shape; at each mask cell output the colour of the key's patterned row at that column, at each non-mask cell the colour of the key's fill row.
gap: Needs mask-select between two key rows broadcast down the columns; key and mask are separate unequal-size objects, not separator panels.

rule: The input is a sequence of equal panels in which an inner shape grows by one cell per step (last panel blank); output is the next panel with the shape grown by one more step.
gap: No sequence extrapolation across panels: infer per-step growth of a shape and render the next term.

rule: All framed window objects share a compartment layout; the colours filled into compartments of any window are pooled by compartment position and every window (whatever its size) gets all its compartments filled accordingly.
gap: Needs part-level object model (window -> compartments) and transfer of compartment fills across windows of different sizes.

rule: A top-left key lists colour pairs a->b; each dot-lattice object of colour a gets every surrounding background cell within its 3x3 neighbourhood filled with b, with overlaps drawn in key-row priority (first row on top).
gap: 2-cell legend exists, but legend must drive a halo/dilation action per object with z-order taken from legend row order.

rule: The sparse lattice of coloured dots is upscaled into a fixed 26x26 canvas of blocks (block size set by lattice dimensions, 2-cell gaps/margins), with horizontally adjacent same-colour cells merged into one block, and vertical merges only for cells not merged horizontally.
gap: Upscale to fixed canvas with variable block size plus merging adjacent equal-colour cells into rectangles; only fixed-factor upscale exists.

rule: The grid is a periodic background pattern divided into panels by yellow/teal lines; a rectangular group of panels is filled with solid colours, and the output is that group downscaled to one cell per panel.
gap: Panel downscale exists; needs restricting to panels of uniform colour (those breaking the periodic pattern) and cropping to their bounding block.

rule: Among vertical teal line segments, one has its top or bottom half coloured maroon; that maroon half is removed and painted onto the same half (top/bottom) of the segment whose length is exactly 2 greater.
gap: Needs ranking/comparison of segment lengths (find the line of length L+2) and transfer of a half-segment recolouring to it.

rule: Within each separator-bounded group of four blocks: if a yellow line divides the group, swap the blocks across that line (left/right or top/bottom); otherwise recolour all blue placeholder blocks to the group's single other colour.
gap: Needs per-group selection between swap-across-divider and fill-placeholders, cued by presence/orientation of a yellow divider line.

rule: Each solid rectangle beside the separator line is mirrored across that line, and the gap between the rectangle and its mirror copy is filled with the separator colour, overwriting noise dots.
gap: Needs per-object reflection across a line object plus bridging fill between original and copy; only global symmetry and same-colour connect exist.

rule: Panels come in left/right pairs, each a background with one shape; the shapes are swapped between the paired panels and each moved shape is drawn in its source panel's background colour, while pairs with equal backgrounds are cleared.
gap: Needs cross-panel object swap with colour remapping to the source background, and a same-background condition that erases both shapes.

rule: A bar of length n in colour c becomes, in raster order across the grid width, runs of length 1,2,...,n,...,2,1 separated by single blank cells, with height as needed.
gap: Needs reading a count (bar length) and generating a counted sequence of runs written in raster (row-wrapped) order.

rule: The grid is three equal panels split by magenta lines; the output panel takes its left column band from panel 1, middle band from panel 2 and right band from panel 3 (bands 2/1/2 wide for 5-wide panels, 2/2/2 for 6-wide).
gap: Panel split exists; output must be assembled from a different column band of each panel (band k from panel k), not a cellwise vote.

rule: Tiles in a separator lattice are either a fixed two-colour pattern or a solid minority-colour block, with grey noise on top; output swaps them: pattern tiles become solid majority colour, solid tiles receive the clean pattern, noise removed.
gap: Needs per-tile type classification under noise and swapping roles of pattern tile and solid tile; no tile-level rewrite with denoising.

rule: Remove the border frame; extend the green band lines across the whole grid, and extend each red segment perpendicular to the band out to the grid edges as rays in the frame colour.
gap: Rays exist, but ray colour must be bound to the frame colour, combined with frame deletion and line extension through the frame.

rule: Drop the left marker column and cyclically shift the remaining rows downward by the row index of the red marker cell in that column.
gap: Toroidal shift exists, but the shift amount must be read from a marker's position (row index) and the marker column removed.

rule: Teal marks on one border: length-1 marks grow to length 2, while length-2 marks are erased and instead cut a 2-cell black notch at the opposite end of the same row/column.
gap: Length-2 marks have a non-local effect (notch at the far opposite edge), beyond radius-4 local change tables.

rule: Crop to the first three rows; the third row becomes a copy of the top row with its non-background colour replaced by magenta (6).
gap: Crop exists; needs one extra step writing row 0 into row 2 with the non-background colour remapped to 6.

rule: Floating shapes fall straight down toward the floor region but stop leaving exactly one empty row between them and the floor (the floor's own shape below each object determines its stop).
gap: Gravity-until-contact exists; needs a stop-one-cell-short offset (resting gap of 1) instead of contact.

rule: Several coloured L/bar fragments scattered on the background are the pieces of a square ring; assemble them (translation only) into a closed square frame, with the background colour filling its interior, and output that square.
gap: Needs puzzle-style assembly: find placements so fragments jointly form a closed rectangular frame.

rule: Split the input into top and bottom halves; output places the top half with a maroon column on its right, then a full maroon row, then the bottom half with a maroon column on its left (halves offset diagonally by one).
gap: Needs splitting the grid into halves and reassembling them with a one-cell offset and a maroon separator cross.

rule: The coloured regions surrounding the central yellow/orange shape exchange colours by a cyclic shift: each region takes the colour of its neighbouring region one step anticlockwise (colours rotate clockwise around the centre); shapes stay fixed.
gap: Needs ordering regions cyclically around a centre and recolouring each with its neighbour's colour (a colour permutation derived from spatial relations).

rule: The top strip holds small glyphs; the framed box shows a partially revealed block-scaled pattern; output is the frame with its interior completed as the glyph (matching the block grid and the revealed blocks) drawn at block scale in the interior colour.
gap: Needs matching a partial block-scaled pattern to a legend glyph (scale-invariant subset match) and rendering the full glyph upscaled inside the frame.

rule: Every object moves straight down by a number of cells equal to its own cell count (clipped at the grid edge).
gap: Translation exists, but displacement must equal each object's size (numerosity-driven move distance).

rule: Each 2-cell segment extends into a full line along its own axis: horizontal pairs fill their whole row, vertical pairs fill their whole column, with row lines drawn over column lines.
gap: Rays exist but in fixed directions; ray axis must follow each segment's orientation, with horizontal lines taking priority over vertical.

rule: Delete every foreign-colour cell/fragment that lies inside or within the concavity of another colour's outline shape; fragments lying outside any shape are kept.
gap: Needs an 'inside / within hull of another object' relation to delete intruders; fill-enclosed only treats fully closed background.

rule: The grey cell moves straight toward the black staircase region until blocked, then slides diagonally along the region's edge while staying adjacent to it, stopping when blocked or when it would lose contact.
gap: Move-until-contact exists; needs a follow-up trajectory sliding diagonally along an obstacle's edge with a contact-based stopping rule.

rule: Each row's middle-colour run slides left through the left-colour region until its right end reaches the leftmost right edge of that run over all rows (or it hits the wall); the displaced left-colour cells reappear on its right.
gap: Needs per-row sliding with a stopping line set globally (min right edge across rows) and displaced-fluid refill; gravity stops only at contact.

rule: Each colour has a fixed glyph shape (consistent across demos) drawn on a horizontal line; erase the existing glyph and, for each pair of border marker cells, draw a line across that row plus that colour's glyph at its usual column.
gap: Needs a cross-demo memory binding colour -> glyph shape/position, retrieved when only marker cells of that colour appear.

rule: Each cluster consists of a blue chevron and a 5-cell coloured plus; the whole cluster moves two cells in the chevron-to-plus direction and the plus is rotated 180 degrees (its colours reversed).
gap: Needs a part-level rule: rigid translation of a composite object plus 180-degree rotation of its coloured sub-part, independent of the specific colours.

rule: The grid holds 3x3 ring nodes (ring colour + centre colour) linked by colour-coded dotted paths; output is one node, apparently the endpoint reached by following the colour-coded path network (exact selection criterion unclear).
gap: Needs graph/pointer following over dotted colour-coded paths between nodes; property-based object selection cannot identify the target node.

rule: The grey comb (solid top plus teeth) jumps to the opposite side of the grid, its teeth sheared diagonally one cell per row back toward its old side, and the floor row under the vacated span turns maroon.
gap: Needs non-rigid shear deformation of an object's teeth plus mirror relocation and a floor mark spanning the remaining width.

rule: Recolour each red shape by its mirror-symmetry axis: symmetric about a horizontal axis -> blue, vertical axis -> green, diagonal axis -> magenta; isolated single cells are erased.
gap: Symmetry key is lost in D8-canonical frames; needs absolute symmetry-axis type (H/V/diagonal) as the key, singletons deleted.

rule: Each isolated dot aligned with a same-colour bar is joined to it by a 1-wide line; the bar gets a 3-cell nub where the line leaves, and the dot becomes a hollow diamond (its four neighbours filled, centre cleared).
gap: Connect-aligned exists for same-colour cells; needs bar-to-dot connection plus decorations at both ends (edge nub, hollow diamond).

rule: In a noisy lattice of separator lines, four line crossings are interrupted (background colour); output is the crop of the rectangle whose corners are those interrupted crossings.
gap: Needs crop delimited by anomalous lattice intersections (gaps in separator lines) rather than fixed corners or selected objects.

rule: Framed boxes containing glyphs are linked in a loop by blue lines; each glyph keeps its shape but takes the colour of the glyph in the next box along the loop (cyclic colour shift).
gap: Needs graph relation 'next box along connecting line loop' and recolouring each glyph by its neighbour's colour.

rule: Each black rectangle touching a grid edge slides straight across to the opposite edge, and every cell in the band it sweeps through is cleaned to orange (grey noise erased).
gap: Needs a slide-to-opposite-border action that ignores obstacles and wipes its swept band; move stops at contact and leaves no trail.

rule: Starting from the top row of red/grey cells, grow a downward triangle: each new cell under a gap is the colour opposite to its upper-left parent when both diagonal parents are coloured, repeated row by row until it narrows out.
gap: Needs iterated application of a local two-parent rule row by row (1-D cellular automaton growth), not one-shot pattern rewriting.

rule: Corner cells act as colour keys; each small two-colour shape whose odd cell matches a corner colour has its two colours swapped, and a glyph in that corner colour is drawn in the matching corner (exact glyph derivation unclear).
gap: Needs corner-marker keys linking shapes to corners, colour swap within shapes, and building a corner glyph from the linked shapes.

rule: Count the cells of each colour and redraw the grid as a sorted histogram: colours in descending frequency fill columns from left to right, each column filled bottom-to-top, preserving all counts.
gap: Needs per-colour counting, sorting by frequency, and re-emitting cells in column-major fill order.

rule: Several overlapping rectangular outlines of different colours are stacked; output is a set of concentric square rings ordered by stacking depth (bottom-most outline outermost, top-most innermost, a single centre cell).
gap: Needs inferring occlusion (drawn-over) order between outlines and rendering them as concentric rings in that order.

rule: Bars hanging from the top edge (with full-height blocks as dividers) are re-encoded into a 10-row output with bars hanging from the top and rising from the bottom; the exact length/position mapping (possibly a counting code) is unclear to me.
gap: Output layout is computed from bar lengths/positions (a numeric re-encoding); no module derives geometry from counted bar lengths.

rule: Normalise the framed object to a 5x5 frame (corners blank) holding the 3x3 window centred on its interior content, then draw two copies in a 15x15 canvas at fixed diagonal offsets (2,2) and (8,8).
gap: Needs resizing a frame object to a canonical size around its content plus fixed-position duplication; no frame-normalising rescale exists.

rule: Replace the scattered object with a horizontal line in its colour whose length equals the object's cell count, centred horizontally on the grid's middle row.
gap: Needs numerosity: count an object's cells and draw a centred line of that length.

rule: Two yellow notched brackets sit in opposite corners; the loose small object is moved to the bottom edge directly beneath the notch of the top bracket (the free bottom corner), keeping its shape.
gap: Needs placement by alignment relation to another object's notch (column of top bracket's gap) plus moving to the bottom edge.

rule: The 6x6 input shows a right-angle corner with arms of length k in one corner; output is a 16x16 canvas with, in the same corner, a right triangle whose arms are length 2k and whose hypotenuse is a diagonal line (outline only).
gap: Needs scaling a corner shape by 2 about its corner and completing it into a triangle with a diagonal hypotenuse, on a fixed canvas.

rule: The grid is a lattice of equal panels; one panel holds a template shape and some panels contain a single black hole cell; the template is copied into every panel with a hole (hole erased), others unchanged.
gap: Needs panel-level copy: write the template panel into all panels flagged by a hole marker; panel ops only vote/overlay into one output.

rule: In a noisy grey/orange grid, grey cells forming diagonal staircase lines (chains of cells stepping diagonally, possibly 2 wide) are recoloured teal; other grey cells stay (exact line criterion unclear).
gap: Needs recognising diagonal/staircase line structures within dense noise; simple diagonal-run detection explains only part of the recoloured cells.

rule: Two 3x3 squares sit in opposite corners; every stray cell of a square's colour is pulled toward that square (straight if aligned with its rows/cols, otherwise diagonally) until it touches it.
gap: Move-until-contact exists but in fixed directions; needs attraction toward the same-colour anchor object (8 directions) per stray cell.

rule: Several objects of different colours are copies of one symmetric template shape with some cells missing; each object is completed to the full template shape in its own colour.
gap: Self-similarity repair must work per object across colours (colour-agnostic template consensus or per-object symmetry), not global grid symmetry.

rule: A pair of grey marker cells near one edge indicates a half: crop the grid to the half (top/bottom if the pair is vertical, left/right if horizontal) containing the markers, and erase the markers to background.
gap: Crop exists for fixed corners; needs half-crop whose axis and side are chosen by a marker pair's orientation and position, markers erased.

rule: The two-colour object (stacked identical halves) swaps its outline and fill colours; its top half is slid right until its bottom-left corner touches the bottom half's top-right corner diagonally, while the bottom half stays.
gap: Needs splitting an object into parts, a relative move of one part to diagonal contact, and swapping its two colours.
